description: Taxonomy of cross-chain / deployment-sensitive constants. Drives manifest tagging (build_coverage_manifest.py via cross_chain_taxonomy.py) and the cross_chain_constants_audit.py detector + review lane. A constant matches a category by name_patterns (case-insensitive substring/regex on the declared name) and/or value_patterns (regex on the assigned literal). The point is to surface values whose correctness depends on WHICH CHAIN the contract is deployed on — the class that produced eval misses #142 (BRIDGE), #133/#135 (token/oracle addr on L2), #320 (MERKLE_ROOT), #469 (block-time), #267 (heartbeat).
_numeric_timing_note: Bare numeric literals (1e18, 100, precision/scale constants) are NEVER tagged on value alone. A numeric constant is tagged timing only when its NAME implies cross-chain/oracle/season/heartbeat semantics (block_time, heartbeat, timeout, window, deadline, sequencer, season). This is the primary false-positive control.

bridge.review_hint: A hardcoded bridge address is chain-specific. Confirm it is the correct canonical bridge on the DEPLOYMENT chain (OP-stack L1StandardBridge vs L2 predeploy 0x4200..0010 vs Arbitrum inbox). A wrong/stale bridge address breaks L1<->L2 message routing and can brick or misroute migration.

messenger.review_hint: Cross-domain messenger address is chain-specific. Verify xDomainMessageSender / message-validation uses the canonical messenger for the deployment chain.

inbox_outbox.review_hint: Arbitrum inbox/outbox or ArbSys address is chain-specific; wrong value breaks retryable/withdrawal message flow.

mailbox.review_hint: Hyperlane mailbox address is per-chain; verify it matches the deployment domain.

endpoint.review_hint: LayerZero endpoint address is per-chain; a wrong endpoint breaks message send/receive.

trusted_remote.review_hint: Trusted-remote / peer / chain-id mapping for a messaging protocol. Wrong remote address or domain id lets messages be spoofed or routed to the wrong chain.

merkle_root.review_hint: A hardcoded merkle root binds the contract to a specific snapshot/distribution. If it is a placeholder, zero, or for the wrong snapshot, migration/claim verification is unusable or wrong. Verify the root matches the intended deployment snapshot.

chain_id.review_hint: A hardcoded chain id (vs block.chainid) bakes a single deployment chain into signatures / replay protection / routing. On any other chain it breaks EIP-712 verification or cross-chain replay separation.

domain_separator.review_hint: EIP-712 domain separator must commit to block.chainid and address(this). A cached/hardcoded domain separator is invalid after a fork or on a different chain.

permit_domain.review_hint: Permit / blueprint typehash + domain. Confirm the typehash matches the struct and the domain is rebuilt per chain; a mismatch breaks permit/blueprint verification.

heartbeat.review_hint: Oracle heartbeat / staleness threshold is feed- and chain-specific (e.g. ETH/USD 1h on L1 vs different on L2). A wrong heartbeat accepts stale prices or rejects fresh ones (DoS).

block_time.review_hint: Block-time assumption (e.g. 12s L1 vs ~2s L2). Code that converts blocks<->seconds or paces auctions/morning-temperature by block time mis-paces on a chain with a different block time.

timestamp_window.review_hint: Timing window/timeout/period. Only cross-chain-relevant when paced by block time or oracle freshness; otherwise likely benign. Confirm units (blocks vs seconds) and chain assumptions.

l1_token.review_hint: L1-side token address used on/after migration. Confirm it is the real L1 token and that the L1<->L2 pairing is correct; a wrong L1 token breaks migration accounting.

l2_token.review_hint: L2-side token address. On a CREATE2/reseed deploy the real L2 token address may differ from a hardcoded vanity constant — verify constant == deployed instance.
examples: BEAN (read on L2 but hardcoded mainnet vanity)

token_mapping.review_hint: L1<->L2 token pairing. A wrong mapping mis-credits migrated balances.

oracle_aggregator.review_hint: Hardcoded Chainlink/oracle aggregator address is per-chain. On another chain it has no code / wrong feed -> latestRoundData reverts or returns 0 -> pricing DoS or manipulation.

sequencer_feed.review_hint: L2 sequencer-uptime feed. Required on L2 to detect sequencer downtime; absent/wrong on L1. Missing/incorrect feed lets stale prices through during downtime.

create2_salt.review_hint: CREATE2 salt. A deterministic address from CREATE2 depends on deployer + initcode + salt; a hardcoded address constant will NOT match a CREATE2-deployed instance if deployer/initcode differ across chains.

proxy_admin.review_hint: Proxy admin / beacon address. Confirm it is the intended governance on the deployment chain.

implementation.review_hint: Implementation/logic address for a proxy/factory. A placeholder address(0) or wrong-chain implementation reverts proxy construction (deploy-DoS) or points at no code.

deployer.review_hint: Deployer/factory address feeding CREATE2 address derivation; differs across chains and changes resulting addresses.

owner.review_hint: Hardcoded owner/governance/multisig. Confirm the address exists and is controlled on the deployment chain (an EOA/multisig on L1 may not be deployed at the same address on L2).

hardcoded_address.review_hint: A hardcoded (non-zero) address literal is chain-specific by construction. Confirm the address has the intended code on the DEPLOYMENT chain (mainnet vanity addresses, CREATE2 instances, and EOAs/multisigs do not generally exist at the same address on another chain).
